neighbours.label: physical how-to instructions for positioning or gripping with the hands or a hand tool (hands under your shoulders, fork firmly in the breast, grab your toes): fires on the placement preposition or grip verb
fire: Lie face down on the mat with your palms flat under your chest, then push up slowly.
Set the carving fork firmly in the top of the roast before you start slicing.
While sitting, bend one leg, grab your ankle and draw it gently toward your hip.
Hold the turkey still with a fork pressed firmly in the drumstick as you cut.
Kneel on the floor with your hands under your knees and round your back.
Reach behind you, grasp your wrist and pull the arm slowly downward.
Plant the tip of the knife firmly in the centre of the melon and press down.
Lie on your back, grab your knees and hug them in toward your chest.
quiet: Lie in the hammock with a good book, then drift off slowly.
Set the oven to a low heat before you start making the sauce.
While waiting, read one chapter and think about what it means for your plan.
Serve the turkey warm with a spoonful of gravy as the guests arrive.
Stay on the trail with your group and watch the weather.
Look behind you, check the mirror and merge slowly into traffic.
Store the melon in the centre of the fridge and eat it within a week.
Rest for a minute, drink some water and breathe out through your nose.

notes: Card: 'hands under your shoulders', 'Place your fork firmly in', 'grasp onto', 'grab your toes' (plus some sympy code at the top). Probes were uneven: 'fork placed firmly in the thigh' 0.93, squeeze the handle 0.32, grab the bar 0.29, palms under thighs 0.27, hands on hips 0.12, skewer into the roast 0.08. A sparse pole; the label may be too broad.
